annotations.description: Sleight of Hand vs Opt on turn 1 is a classic sequencing question. Opt's scry 1 then draw lets you see one card and either keep or bottom it, then draw the next. Sleight of Hand looks at two cards and picks one. Generally Sleight of Hand digs slightly deeper (sees 2 cards vs Opt's effective 2 cards but with different selection). However, Opt is an instant and could be saved for the opponent's end step to keep mana open for responses. On turn 1 with only 1 mana available and no interactive spells that cost U in hand (Three Steps Ahead costs more), there's no meaningful advantage to holding up mana. The choice between these two cantrips is extremely close and largely preference-dependent. Sleight of Hand is a reasonable choice here since there's nothing to hold up mana for.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sleight of Hand on turn 1 main phase
annotations.betterLine: Could have cast Opt at end of opponent's turn to preserve information advantage, though with no interaction available this turn the difference is negligible

annotations.description: Discarded Multiversal Passage, their only land in hand, when they have 5 lands on board and need to reach 9 mana to cast Sunderflock (no Elementals in play to reduce cost). Every land drop matters for reaching their win condition.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Multiversal Passage and Winternight Stories
annotations.betterLine: Discard Burst Lightning (low impact vs UW control with no creatures) and Winternight Stories instead, keeping Multiversal Passage for the crucial 6th land drop to progress toward casting Sunderflock.

annotations.description: With Winternight Stories' discard clause ('discard two cards unless you discard a creature card'), Sonnet Teach chose to discard Spider-Sense (non-creature) as the first card, forcing them to discard a second card as well. They have two Eddymurk Crabs in hand, so discarding one creature card would have satisfied the condition with only one discard, saving an entire card.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Spider-Sense (non-creature) as first discard, requiring a second discard to fulfill Winternight Stories' condition.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a single Eddymurk Crab (creature card) to satisfy Winternight Stories' condition, keeping one more card in hand. With two Crabs in hand and the cost already reduced to ~2 mana, losing one copy is much less costly than losing two non-creature cards.

annotations.description: Gem25P Stoic declined to activate Fountainport's abilities during their main phase when they had 8 lands available and nothing else to do with their mana. They could have used Fountainport to create a Fish token ({3}, {T}, Pay 1 life) to start building a board presence, or created a Treasure token ({4}, {T}) for future mana flexibility. With an Eddymurk Crab threatening them and no creatures of their own, generating any board presence or resources would be valuable. The reasoning mentions 'no castable spells' but overlooks that Fountainport's activated abilities are available and Stock Up (3 mana) is in hand and castable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Fountainport or casting any spells, despite having 8 untapped lands and Stock Up in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Stock Up to dig for answers (like Day of Judgment or more removal), then activate Fountainport to create a Fish token or Treasure token with remaining mana. At minimum, activate Fountainport for a token before passing.

annotations.description: Casting Get Lost during their own combat phase rather than waiting until the opponent's upkeep/draw step or end of opponent's turn. This unnecessarily uses mana now, leaving less mana available for counterspells during the opponent's turn, and gives away information about hand contents.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Get Lost on Eddymurk Crab during their own combat phase
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn with all mana open, then cast Get Lost during opponent's end step or upkeep, keeping maximum mana available for No More Lies or Spell Snare during the opponent's main phase

annotations.description: Discarded Eddymurk Crab which costs only {U}{U} with 12 instants/sorceries in graveyard, keeping Sunderflock which costs {9} without any Elemental in play to reduce its cost. The Eddymurk Crab was immediately castable as a 5/5 flash threat, while Sunderflock is essentially a dead card without an Elemental on board. Furthermore, Eddymurk Crab on the battlefield would have reduced Sunderflock's cost to {2}{U}{U}, making the sequencing even worse.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Eddymurk Crab to keep Sunderflock
annotations.betterLine: Discard Sunderflock and keep Eddymurk Crab, which is immediately castable for {U}{U} as a powerful 5/5 flash creature with ETB tap ability

annotations.description: With 2 untapped Steam Vents (producing RR or UR), Sonnet Teach passed with nothing and then had to discard 2 cards from a 9-card hand. They had 3 Burst Lightnings in hand - casting 2 at the opponent's face would deal 4 damage, reduce hand to exactly 7 (no discard needed), and add instants to graveyard (reducing Eddymurk Crab/Sunderflock costs). Instead they wasted 2 mana and lost 2 cards to discard.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 2 untapped lands, then discarded 2 cards to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Cast two Burst Lightnings targeting the opponent (RR from two Steam Vents) to deal 4 damage, avoid discarding, and grow the graveyard for future cost reduction.

annotations.description: Gem25P Stoic declined to activate Restless Anchorage to attack when the opponent was completely tapped out. With Sunken Citadel (producing 2W for land abilities) and Floodfarm Verge available, they could animate Restless Anchorage (1WU) and attack for 2 flying damage plus create a Map token, with zero risk since the opponent has all lands tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Restless Anchorage, missing a free attack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Anchorage using Sunken Citadel and Floodfarm Verge, then attack for 2 flying damage and generate a Map token.

annotations.description: In a control mirror, Restless Anchorage is a premium win condition that can attack through counter-heavy boards. Playing Sunken Citadel instead means delaying the deployment of a key threat. The Sunken Citadel's double-mana for land abilities (Fountainport) is a marginal advantage compared to having a creature-land that can pressure the opponent's life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Sunken Citadel (choosing Blue) as land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Anchorage as the land drop. It provides a repeatable evasive threat (2/3 flyer) that is critical for closing out control mirrors, and it also generates Map tokens when attacking.

annotations.description: Discarded the last Eddymurk Crab when it would cost only {U}{U} to cast (7 instants/sorceries in graveyard reducing its cost by 7). With Eddymurk Crab on the battlefield (MV 7), Sunderflock would also cost only {U}{U}. This Crab+Sunderflock line is the deck's primary win condition. By discarding all 4 Eddymurk Crabs, Sunderflock now costs a full 9 mana with no discount enabler.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded the last Eddymurk Crab to pay for Winternight Stories' creature discard cost.
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Sunderflocks instead, preserving the Eddymurk Crab which costs {U}{U} and enables the remaining Sunderflock to also cost {U}{U}, creating a devastating 2-creature sequence for just 4 mana total.

annotations.description: Discarding Abandon Attachments (which can turn any dead card into 2 fresh cards for just 2 mana) over a third copy of Spell Snare (a narrow counter that only hits exactly 2-mana spells). Already keeping one Spell Snare plus Spell Pierce for countermagic coverage.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded 2 Opts, 1 Spell Snare, and Abandon Attachments, keeping 2 Spell Snares
annotations.betterLine: Discard 2 Opts and 2 Spell Snares, keeping Abandon Attachments for flexible card advantage alongside 1 Spell Snare and 1 Spell Pierce for counter coverage

annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating Restless Anchorage or taking any action.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} to make it a 2/3 flying creature and attack for lethal against the opponent at 2 life.

annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Anchorage (it enters tapped this turn but can be activated next turn for {1}{W}{U} to attack as a 2/3 flyer for lethal).

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life. Gem25P Stoic has Restless Anchorage on the battlefield and 8 lands available. Activating Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} would create a 2/3 flyer. However, the player chose to pass without doing anything this main phase. While they mention activating it during opponent's end step, that doesn't help - they need to attack with it, which means they need to activate it on their own turn (ideally before combat). Since this is postcombat main, the attack window has already passed this turn. The real mistake was likely not activating Restless Anchorage before combat to attack for lethal with the 2/3 flyer. Passing here without casting anything meaningful (like Elspeth who could also create tokens) wastes a turn when the opponent is at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without taking any action in postcombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Should have activated Restless Anchorage before combat (in precombat main) to attack with a 2/3 flyer for lethal against the 2-life opponent. At this point in postcombat, casting Elspeth, Storm Slayer to create soldier tokens (doubled to two 1/1s) would set up lethal next turn with multiple threats. Alternatively, Three Steps Ahead to draw cards and find burn could also be considered.

annotations.description: At 2 life with 7 lands (only one tapped), Sonnet Teach has Winternight Stories in graveyard available to Harmonize. With creatures in the graveyard (Eddymurk Crab x4, Sunderflock x2), tapping a creature could reduce the Harmonize cost. However, there are no creatures on board to tap. The Harmonize cost is {4}{U} = 5 mana, and with 7 lands (6 untapped), this is castable. Drawing 3 cards and discarding a creature could help find more answers. That said, the player has a reasonable hand with multiple counterspells (2x Spell Snare, Spell Pierce) and interaction (Into the Flood Maw, Burst Lightning), so holding up countermagic at 2 life is also defensible. The decision to pass without casting anything is reasonable given the need to hold up counters at such low life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting anything, holding up counterspell mana.
annotations.betterLine: Could have considered casting Winternight Stories via Harmonize for {4}{U} to dig deeper for threats while still leaving {U} open for Spell Pierce, though this would tap out of Spell Snare range. Holding up counters at 2 life is defensible.

annotations.description: Failed to play Island from hand before casting Sunderflock. At 2 life, maximizing available mana is critical for holding up protection spells. Playing the land first is strictly better sequencing - it provides an additional mana source for subsequent turns and potentially allows holding up more interaction after casting the threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sunderflock without first playing the Island from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first, then cast Sunderflock. This gives an extra land in play for future turns to better hold up counterspells like Spell Pierce or Spell Snare while at a precarious 2 life.

annotations.description: Gem25P Stoic passed their entire postcombat main phase with 8 untapped lands, doing nothing while the opponent sits at 2 life with all lands tapped and no board. They even had to discard to hand size, wasting cards. The reasoning incorrectly states 'the game should be over' when the opponent is still alive at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, then discarded Seam Rip and Get Lost to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Elspeth, Storm Slayer (5 mana) while opponent is tapped out and can't interact. Elspeth's +1 creates 2 soldier tokens (doubled), immediately threatening lethal next turn against an opponent at 2 life. Still has 3 mana up for No More Lies or Spell Snare to protect Elspeth on the opponent's turn.
